sections.content: Transactions group statements so they all succeed or all roll back — bank transfers need debit+credit atomic, never half-done.
ACID: Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Consistency (constraints hold), Isolation (concurrent txns do not interfere), Durability (committed data survives crashes). Isolation levels trade safety for speed.
Key points: BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK control the boundary, deadlocks happen under concurrency (retry logic helps), and read committed is the common default.
